proof:
Source: the printed proof of Simon, Ch. 2, Theorem 1.5 (pp. 42-44), with the measure-theoretic details filled in. The parent proof (step 1) cites this theorem; it is proved here once.
Notation: L^n = volume on R^n; |.| Euclidean norm; for k >= 1 write S_k := {x : k - 1 <= |x| < k} (Borel, bounded, pairwise disjoint, union R^n). For x where f is differentiable write Df(x) for its derivative (a linear map R^n -> R).
1. (Rademacher.) The set B := {x : f is differentiable at x} is Borel (Mathlib measurableSet_of_differentiableAt) and L^n(R^n \ B) = 0 by Rademacher's theorem (Mathlib LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt; SimonGMT Chapter02.rademacher_ae_differentiableAt). The map x -> Df(x) = fderiv R f x is Borel measurable (Mathlib measurable_fderiv).
2. (Lusin on bounded pieces.) Fix k >= 1. A_k := B cap S_k is Borel with L^n(A_k) < infinity. L^n restricted to a bounded set is a finite Borel measure on a metric space, hence weakly regular (Mathlib Measure.WeaklyRegular.of_pseudoMetrizableSpace_of_isFiniteMeasure). By weak regularity choose a closed set C_k^0 contained in A_k with L^n(A_k \ C_k^0) < eps 2^{-k-2}/(n+1) (Mathlib MeasurableSet.exists_isClosed_sdiff_lt). For q = 1..n apply Lusin's theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 1.17; SimonGMT Chapter01.exists_isClosed_continuousOn_of_measurable) to the Borel real function x -> Df(x)(e_q) on A_k with tolerance eps 2^{-k-2}/(n+1): this gives a closed set C_k^q contained in A_k with L^n(A_k \ C_k^q) < eps 2^{-k-2}/(n+1) and x -> Df(x)(e_q) continuous on C_k^q. Put C_k := C_k^0 cap C_k^1 cap ... cap C_k^n (for n = 0 this is just C_k^0). Then C_k is closed, contained in A_k, L^n(A_k \ C_k) < eps 2^{-k-2}, and Df restricted to C_k is continuous (a map into the finite-dimensional space of linear maps R^n -> R is continuous iff its coordinates Df(.)(e_q) are; for n = 0 that space is a single point). Put C := union_k C_k. Since C_k is contained in the bounded set S_k, every bounded set meets only finitely many C_k; hence C is closed (locally finite union of closed sets) and Df restricted to C is continuous (each point has a neighbourhood meeting only finitely many of the closed sets C_k, and Df is continuous on each of them, so the pasting lemma applies). Moreover C is contained in B and L^n(R^n \ C) <= L^n(R^n \ B) + sum_k L^n(A_k \ C_k) <= sum_{k>=1} eps 2^{-k-2} = eps/4.
3. (The remainder functions.) For x != y in C put R(x, y) := (f(y) - f(x) - Df(x)(y - x))/|y - x|. For k >= 1 and x in C let phi_k(x) := sup({0} union {|R(x, y)| : y in C, 0 < |y - x| < 1/k}); put phi_k := 0 off C. Since f is K-Lipschitz, |R(x, y)| <= K + ||Df(x)||, so 0 <= phi_k(x) < infinity; phi_{k+1} <= phi_k; and phi_k(x) -> 0 as k -> infinity for every x in C, because f is differentiable at x (C is contained in B). Measurability: let D be a countable dense subset of C. For fixed x in C the set {y in C : 0 < |y - x| < 1/k} is relatively open in C, hence D is dense in it, and y -> |R(x, y)| is continuous on it (f continuous, denominator nonzero); therefore phi_k(x) = sup({0} union {|R(x, y)| : y in D, 0 < |y - x| < 1/k}). For each fixed y in D, x -> |R(x, y)| times the indicator of {x in C : 0 < |y - x| < 1/k} is Borel (Df Borel, f continuous, C closed). So phi_k is a countable supremum of Borel functions, hence Borel.
4. (Egorov on bounded pieces.) Fix k >= 1. C cap S_k has finite measure, phi_j are Borel and phi_j -> 0 pointwise on C cap S_k. By Egorov's theorem (Mathlib tendstoUniformlyOn_of_ae_tendsto' applied to L^n restricted to C cap S_k) there is a Borel set E_k contained in C cap S_k with L^n((C cap S_k) \ E_k) < eps 2^{-k-2} and phi_j -> 0 uniformly on E_k as j -> infinity. Put A_0 := union_k E_k. Then L^n(C \ A_0) <= sum_k eps 2^{-k-2} = eps/4, and since a bounded set meets only finitely many S_k, phi_j -> 0 uniformly on every bounded subset of A_0 (a finite union of sets of uniform convergence).
5. (A closed set.) For each k choose, by weak regularity of L^n restricted to the bounded set E_k (Mathlib MeasurableSet.exists_isClosed_sdiff_lt), a closed set F_k contained in E_k with L^n(E_k \ F_k) < eps 2^{-k-2}. Put A := union_k F_k; A is closed (F_k is contained in S_k, so the union is locally finite), A is contained in A_0, contained in C, contained in B, and L^n(A_0 \ A) <= eps/4. Hence L^n(R^n \ A) <= L^n(R^n \ C) + L^n(C \ A_0) + L^n(A_0 \ A) <= 3 eps/4 < eps.
6. (Whitney's hypothesis.) Let h := f and xi := Df on A. h is continuous on A (f Lipschitz) and xi is continuous on A (A contained in C, step 2). Let K' be a compact subset of A and eta > 0. K' is bounded, so by step 4 there is j with phi_j < eta on K'. Then for x in K' and y in A with |y - x| < 1/j: if y != x, |f(y) - f(x) - Df(x)(y - x)| = |R(x, y)| |y - x| <= phi_j(x)|y - x| <= eta|y - x| (y is in A, contained in C); if y = x the inequality is trivial. This is exactly the hypothesis (*) of Whitney's extension theorem (Simon Ch. 2, 1.6), i.e. HasWhitneyC1Compatibility A h xi in SimonGMT (continuous value, continuous derivative, remainder with delta = 1/j).
7. (Whitney extension and conclusion.) By Whitney's extension theorem (Simon Ch. 2, Theorem 1.6; SimonGMT Chapter02.exists_contDiff_one_extension_of_whitney) there is g in C^1(R^n) (ContDiff R 1 g) with g = f on A and HasFDerivAt g (Df(a)) a for every a in A; hence Dg(a) = Df(a) for a in A. Therefore {f != g} union {Df != Dg} is contained in R^n \ A, whose measure is < eps by step 5. (If A is empty the extension is any C^1 function, e.g. 0, and the same inclusion holds.) This proves the claim.
key_steps: Rademacher: f is differentiable off an L^n-null Borel set B^c, and Df is Borel
Lusin on the bounded shells: a closed C contained in B with Df continuous on C and L^n(R^n \ C) <= eps/4
The difference quotients phi_k (countable sup over a dense subset, hence Borel) decrease to 0 on C
Egorov on the shells: phi_k -> 0 uniformly on bounded subsets of A_0, L^n(C \ A_0) <= eps/4
Inner regularity: a closed A contained in A_0 with L^n(R^n \ A) < eps
Whitney's C^1 compatibility holds on A; Whitney extension gives g in C^1 with g = f and Dg = Df on A
